rule: **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding. A definition that edges reach is listed in `nodes`, including body-less member declarations of scanned types (interface/trait/protocol methods) and module-level bindings that hold a function. A high edge's callee is always in `nodes`. **Java / Kotlin / C# / Groovy / Scala**: package/namespace-qualified: `com.x.C#m`; an external type is qualified through its explicit import. Kotlin top-level functions `com.x.f`. A Groovy script (a file with top-level code or functions) is a class named after the file: its functions are `pkg.Script#f`, its top-level code `pkg.Script#run`. **Implicitly imported names are qualified**: Java/Scala/Groovy `java.lang.String`, Groovy's default imports (`java.util.List`, `groovy.lang.Closure`, …). With exactly one on-demand import (`import a.b.*`), a simple type name that is not in the file's package, not imported singly and not a java.lang type is `a.b.Name` (medium); with more than one such import it stays unqualified, low. Honest low (do not resolve by guessing): calls resolved only at runtime through a closure delegate (Groovy), query/DSL names read by a macro (Ecto `field`, `type`), and types reachable only through more than one wildcard import.
source: KNOWN_GAP: import renames and several-wildcard imports are not resolved
notes: `import util.{Helper => H}` is an alias; C1 requires every reference through an alias to use the definition's ID, util.Helper#…, never H#…. Widget is reachable through two wildcard imports (model._, other._), but the scan supplies exactly one definition of it (model.Widget; package other is scanned and defines only Gadget), so resolution is by definition, not a guess: model.Widget, high. The several-wildcard 'stays unqualified, low' ruling (Decisions 2026-10-29) is the fallback for a name the scan does not define; that reading is an inference, recorded here. call_type convention used throughout: a call on a receiver (written, or the implicit this/object of a bare member call) is `method`; a call of a named nested function or an unresolved bare name is `direct`; `new`/super/this constructor calls are `constructor`; calls through function values are `callback`. SPEC lists the call_type values but does not define direct vs method beyond this.
